goldens.comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.

While the imports are lazy (they return promises), the import() calls are all invoked when the appStore object is created. However, this is actually an improvement over the previous static imports which loaded everything synchronously. This is a legitimate architectural concern about the lazy loading pattern, though the severity is debatable since dynamic imports are still more efficient than static imports.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {` at line 125 in wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts. Using forEach with an async callback means the promises returned by the async function are discarded - forEach doesn't await them. This means the calendar deletion operations (via `await getCalendar(...)` and `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)`) will execute asynchronously without being awaited, so the function can complete and return before these operations finish. Any errors thrown by these async operations won't be caught by the surrounding try block. This is a real bug introduced by the change from synchronous to async getCalendar.
